# Work Breakdown Structure

Hierarchical decomposition of a project's total scope into progressively smaller deliverables, until
the leaves are units small enough to estimate, assign and schedule. Everything else in
[[computer-project-management]] — dependencies, resourcing, [[critical-path-method|critical path]],
cost — hangs off this one structure. It is the spine, not a diagram.

## The shape used

Three levels plus a milestone layer, held constant across all five lab stages:

| Level | Count | Example |
|---|:--:|---|
| Phases (level 1) | 3 | Preparatory · Execution · Finalization |
| Task groups (level 2) | 9 | *System requirements analysis*, *Platform development*, *Testing phase* |
| Working tasks (level 3) | 26 | *Market research Europe–Asia routes*, *Backend API development*, *User acceptance testing* |
| Control-point milestones | 7 | one 0-day checkpoint closing each main block of work |

Milestones are not a fourth level of work — they are zero-duration markers attached to the outline
so that completion becomes a reportable event. That is what makes
[[schedule-baseline-and-variance]] readable per phase rather than only in aggregate.

## Two properties worth naming

**The outline is built before it is linked.** `docs/images/wbs-initial.png` shows the lab-2 task
list with every task still starting on day one — decomposition first, sequencing second. Only once
the leaves exist do FS/SS/FF dependencies get drawn between them.

**The structure survives every later change.** Task counts move (29 practice → 38 → 45) as
milestones and re-decomposition arrive, but the 3/9/26 skeleton is the same object in lab 7–8's
report as in lab 2's plan. A WBS that had to be rebuilt each lab would not be a baseline for
anything.

## Practised on a throwaway first

Lab 1 exists only to learn the mechanics — indenting, durations, the first Finish-to-Start links —
on a plan that is explicitly discarded:

> "This file is a throwaway sandbox, not the Export/Import project. It exists to practise the"
> — Computer Project Management/lab1_WBS_Practice/README.md, 2026-07-10

The same separation shows up as directory names in [[numbered-stages-in-directory-names]]: the
sandbox and the real artefact live in different folders and are never merged.

## What the repo does not do

- **No 100 % rule stated.** The principle that a parent's children must sum to exactly the parent's
  scope is never named, though the rolled-up durations in the lab 7–8 report behave as if it holds.
- **No WBS dictionary.** Tasks are named but not defined; there are no entry/exit criteria, no
  acceptance criteria, no owner per work package outside the resource assignment.
- **No decomposition rule.** Nothing records why 26 leaves rather than 15 or 60, or what stopping
